sources.title: Mission Archéologique France-Madagascar, Les Vazimba et le peuplement malgache
sources.note: French Ministry of Culture project page. Explorer, funerary archaeology, innovative tools, and occupation metadata distinguish open questions from thirteenth-to-nineteenth-century evidence.

sources.title: Robertine Rajoelinoro, Les traces matérielles de la présence vazimba d’Analamanga au XVIe siècle
sources.note: Introduction paragraphs 1 to 3 and section I explain source scarcity, category disagreements, temporal dilation, multiple Vazimba meanings, and the chiefly fourteenth-to-sixteenth-century evidence base.

sources.title: Heiske et al., Genetic evidence and historical theories of the Asian and African origins of the present Malagasy population
sources.note: Abstract, Historical Elements, group-assignment caution, admixture sections, and conclusion concern modern population history and genetics, not target-period healing or care.

sources.title: Serva and Pasquini, Dialects of Madagascar
sources.note: Abstract and sections 3.2 to 3.3 present a model-based 623 to 681 CE linguistic estimate and caution that Vazimba has mythic, political, and non-ethnic meanings.

sources.title: Wright et al., The Evolution of Settlement Systems in the Region of Vohémar, Northeast Madagascar
sources.note: Chapter 7 pages 25 to 39, especially 31 to 32 and 38 to 39, documents the eighth-to-tenth-century Ampasimahavelona phase, artifacts, food remains, and tentative settlement layout.

sources.title: Crowther et al., Ancient crops provide first archaeological signature of the westward Austronesian expansion
sources.note: Table 1, Table S1, Results, and SI Text distinguish eighth-century Ampasimahavelona with zero crops from Mahilaka deposits dated about 1050 to 1350 and irrigation by roughly 1100.

sources.title: Hixon et al., Late Holocene spread of pastoralism coincides with endemic megafaunal extinction on Madagascar
sources.note: Results section 3a and Discussion date directly tested introduced sheep and zebu no earlier than roughly 890 to 990 CE, after the atlas interval.

sources.title: Jean-Pierre Domenichini, Vazimba et esprits helo : la profondeur chronologique
sources.note: Sections 1 to 7 and conclusion document later and living uses of Vazimba for powerful ancestral beings and grandees without turning them into target-period biology.

sources.title: Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, Malagasy
sources.note: Discovering the language identifies Malagasy as Austronesian, notes African and Asian lexical histories, regional varieties, Sorabe, and the nineteenth-century Latin writing tradition.

sources.title: Republic of Madagascar, 1992 Constitution in Malagasy
sources.note: Official Gazette page 2184 supplies the exact modern Malagasy sentence “Ny teny malagasy no tenim-pirenena.”

sources.title: Republic of Madagascar, 1992 Constitution in French
sources.note: Official French counterpart supplies “Le malgache est la langue nationale,” securing the English translation of the modern sample.

sources.title: Alexander Adelaar, Asian Roots of the Malagasy: A Linguistic Perspective
sources.note: Pages 325 to 356 compare Malagasy with Southeast Barito, Malay, Javanese, and Bantu forms and reconstruct layered language contact rather than a single isolated origin.

sources.title: Chantal Radimilahy, Madagascar: From Initial Settlement to the Growth of Kingdoms
sources.note: Abstract and chapter pages 942 to 954 frame first settlement, late-first-millennium trade, later urbanization, and later state formation as different analytical stages.

sources.title: Pierron et al., Genomic landscape of human diversity across Madagascar
sources.note: Abstract, introduction, results, and discussion show heterogeneous African and Asian ancestry, reject a simple Vazimba genetic label, and call for ancient DNA.

sources.title: Pierron et al., Genome-wide evidence of Austronesian-Bantu admixture and cultural reversion in a hunter-gatherer group of Madagascar
sources.note: Abstract and admixture results show Mikea genomes resemble other sampled Malagasy populations, blocking their use as unchanged biological Vazimba proxies.

sources.title: Kusuma et al., Malagasy Genetic Ancestry Comes from an Historical Malay Trading Post in Southeast Borneo
sources.note: Abstract and discussion identify complex Banjar-related Asian ancestry and warn that admixture dates mark contact processes rather than first arrival.

sources.title: Virah-Sawmy et al., Montane rainforest dynamics under changes in climate and human impact during the past millennia in northern Madagascar
sources.note: Abstract, methods, and discussion reconstruct drought, fire, vegetation, and human impact, with strong local signals mainly after the atlas interval; the study is not a sanitation record.

sources.title: Andriatsitohaina et al., Rain Forest Fragmentation and Environmental Dynamics on Nosy Be Island at 1300 cal BP
sources.note: Results and discussion infer intensified human impact around 1300 calibrated BP while acknowledging that associated archaeological remains at Nosy Be lack direct dates.

sources.title: Alexander Adelaar, Seventeenth century texts as a key to Malagasy linguistic and ethnic history
sources.note: Research registry abstract dates Houtman’s 1603 wordbook and the earliest Sorabe texts to the seventeenth century; it supplies no written school record from 600 to 800.

sources.title: Pierron et al., Strong selection during the last millennium for African ancestry in the admixed population of Madagascar
sources.note: Abstract and introduction analyze modern genomes and disease-related Duffy blood-group variation during the last millennium, not target-period medicine or named communities.

sources.title: University of Michigan Press, The Evolution of Settlement Systems in the Region of Vohémar
sources.note: Publisher description identifies the four-season survey, seventh- and eighth-century estuarine villages, a rock shelter with microlithic tools, and the later port sequence.

sources.title: Razafindrazaka et al., MadInter funerary-archaeology project abstract
sources.note: BMSAP 37 supplement abstract pages S10 to S50 describes collective burials, biological profiles, kinship, and sixteenth-to-nineteenth-century contexts, outside this card’s interval.

sources.title: European Commission CORDIS, Final Report Summary for the Sealinks Project
sources.note: Official project report describes 27 excavated sites, multidisciplinary methods, early Indian Ocean contacts, migration, trade, and archaeobotanical findings.

sources.title: Robert Dewar and Henry Wright, The Culture History of Madagascar
sources.note: Journal of World Prehistory 7, pages 427 to 430 and later phase summaries catalog dated settlements, stone artifacts, ceramics, subsistence, and exchange without assigning target-period gender or age roles.

sources.title: Sealinks Project, Book of Abstracts
sources.note: Pages 7 to 8 describe Vohémar survey, pottery and shell scatters, eighth-century villages, Ambohiposa tools, missing bones, and later Lakaton’i Anja work.

sources.title: Dewar and Wright, A chronology for late prehistoric Madagascar
sources.note: University research record summarizes a database of 278 age determinations and the need to evaluate archaeological chronology systematically.

sources.title: University of Cambridge repository, Ancient crops provide first archaeological signature of the westward Austronesian expansion
sources.note: Institutional repository record identifies the published peer-reviewed archaeobotanical study, its authors, and its Madagascar settlement and crop-movement scope.
